notes: Independent review of r-20261008T063157699792-mast-saddle-voltage-units at head 9424ff401b6a1efc2197dd3fb70fc603c85523bc against base 1d34f09cb6d4f14fdfbe6760f5a48ef3224b5903. The node answers the question the admission node left open: whether the 23 cohort shots without voltage metadata can be calibrated. It adds benchmarks/mast_saddle_voltage_units.py, which reads per-signal units from the level-1 store, treats an arbitrary label as supplying no conversion, and conditions any gain transfer on every known-unit control reproducing both gain and waveform within two percent through a direct coil-pickup model. Its verdict is a measured refusal: 0 of 36 loops validate on the three known-unit controls (25818/25828/25836, 108 Volt-labelled signals), the 23 target shots' 368 available signals retain unknown units, no traversal sign is promoted and the admission fit is not rerun. Every manifest claim reconciles with the logs: the receipt revises at 609b5fb0, its summary equals the benchmark's own printed line in the all_debug job 1282033 (EXIT=0), the negative control reddens three head-green tests at EXIT=1, and the 23-shot set matches the admission node's own refusal set exactly. Because the benchmark is new there is no baseline arm; the added-failure difference is the empty after_suite failure set, so zero failures are added. Two follow-on findings (a duplicated coil-outline/response construction in pickup_geometry; a private cross-module import of _resolve_raw) restate the plan's extend-the-owners principle but do not block: this node's own scope is the unit/gain question and core: it neither owns the admission path nor re-runs it. The plan's next steps (sourcing the historical XMB acquisition conversion, or validating a pickup model with passive response) remain this node's declared follow-on.
